why_not: I already have a working workflow and do not want another resident app sitting in my menu bar.
I already have a bash alias for ffmpeg and imagemagick. It is hard to justify spending $19 when my terminal is always open.
I only convert a file once a month. Free web tools or Apple Preview are good enough for my occasional use.

Granting accessibility permissions to an indie app makes me slightly nervous on my corporate machine.
I understand it is local, but $19 still feels high when there are dozens of free tools online.
why_yes: Clean, fast, and does exactly what I need without opening heavy software.
I convert webp to png and make gifs five times a day. Having it right on the cursor dial saves me ten minutes every single day.
I cannot risk client NDAs with web uploaders like CloudConvert. $19 for an offline tool is a complete no-brainer.
